name: Tocasia
description: An archaeologist, friend of the brothers' father, who taught Urza and Mishra and died inadvertently during the Brotherhood's End.

description_citations.text: "Urza". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Urza and Mishra, with their master Tocasia, explore the sacred cave of Koilos; Urza falls behind in the Hall of Tagsin and finds the Mightstone.
timeline.quote: Urza fell behind in the Hall of Tagsin, where he discovered the remarkable Mightstone.

citation.text: Mightstone (Antiquities, 1994), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: As children, Tocasia takes the brothers to Koilos, where Mishra discovers the weakstone.
timeline.quote: Mishra discovered the mysterious weakstone.

citation.text: Weakstone (Antiquities, 1994), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Two orphans from Argive, Urza and Mishra, are brought to Tocasia's school and spend years learning the secrets of the Thran.
timeline.quote: They live for many years at the school, learning the secrets of the Thran.

citation.text: "Antiquities War", section "Volume 1". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The brothers fly Tocasia in the ornithopter, crash near the Caves of Koilos and find two powerstones; each craves both and they begin to mistrust each other.
timeline.quote: Urza takes the Mightstone , and Mishra the Weakstone .

citation.text: "Antiquities War", section "Volume 1". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The brothers' contest ends in an explosion that kills Tocasia and many others, and they split ways.
timeline.quote: Their confrontation ends in an explosion, that kills Tocasia and many others.

citation.text: "Antiquities War", section "Volume 2". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: When their father falls ill, Urza and Mishra are sent to study at Tocasia's archaeological dig.
timeline.quote: he sent them away to his old friend, Tocasia

citation.text: "Brothers' War", section "Background". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The brothers' rivalry over the halves causes a falling-out and Tocasia's accidental death.
timeline.quote: the inadvertent death of Tocasia

citation.text: "Brothers' War", section "Background". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After their parents' deaths, the brothers Urza and Mishra come to an archeological school, where their tale begins.
timeline.quote: Following the deaths of their parents, the two brothers came to one of the archeological schools.

citation.text: "Excerpts from The Antiquities War", section "Introduction". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In the contest between the brothers Tocasia is killed and her school is probably destroyed; each keeps one stone.
timeline.quote: As a result of the contest, Tocasia was killed and her school was most likely destroyed.

citation.text: "Excerpts from The Antiquities War", section "Volume 1: The Story of Urza and Mishra". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Mishra builds his stronghold on the foundation of the School of Tocasia in the Kher Ridges.
timeline.quote: Mishra's stronghold was found in the Kher Ridges -- built on the foundation of the School of Tocasia.

citation.text: "Excerpts from The Antiquities War", section "Volume 2: The Urza-Mishra War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Urza and Mishra uncover the stones in the Hall of Tagsin, each taking one, which reactivates the gate to Phyrexia.
timeline.quote: Urza took the Mightstone and Mishra the Weakstone, unwittingly reactivating the gate to Phyrexia.

citation.text: "Mightstone and Weakstone", section "The Brothers' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The jealous brothers use the stones against each other and accidentally kill Tocasia, then separate.
timeline.quote: accidentally killing Tocasia when she tried to calm them

citation.text: "Mightstone and Weakstone", section "The Brothers' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Mishra and Urza are born; years later their father dies after sending them to apprentice with Tocasia.
timeline.quote: they remained with her

citation.text: "Mishra", section "Early Years". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia, Urza and Mishra fly to the Thran city Koilos, find a great machine, and an explosion leaves each brother holding half of the powerstone.
timeline.quote: each brother was holding a half of the great stone in their hand

citation.text: "Mishra", section "Apprenticeship to Tocasia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Mishra confronts Urza while drunk and tries to take his stone; Tocasia is killed caught between the stones' powers and Mishra flees.
timeline.quote: she was caught between the powers surging from the two stones and died

citation.text: "Mishra", section "Apprenticeship to Tocasia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia takes Urza and Mishra, about sixteen, on a pilgrimage to the Caves of Koilos where they find the Mightstone and Weakstone.
timeline.quote: Urza discovered the Mightstone, and Mishra, the Weakstone.

citation.text: "The Brothers' War (article)", section "Text". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After the pilgrimage the brothers grow apart, becoming jealous of Tocasia's attention and guarding their secrets.
timeline.quote: They became increasingly jealous of Tocasia’s attention.

citation.text: "The Brothers' War (article)", section "Text". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia dies, removing the brothers' last restraining influence, and the battle is joined in earnest.
timeline.quote: Shortly thereafter, Tocasia died, ridding the brothers of their final restraining influence.

citation.text: "The Brothers' War (article)", section "Text". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Urza and Mishra are sent to Tocasia's archaeological dig after their father falls ill.
timeline.quote: he sent them away to his old friend, Tocasia , to serve as students at her archaeological dig

citation.text: "Urza", section "Early years". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At the Caves of Koilos the brothers break the powerstone sealing Phyrexia in two, and Tocasia dies inadvertently in the resulting Brotherhood's End.
timeline.quote: in their haste to grab the stone before the other brother, they broke it in two

citation.text: "Urza", section "Apprenticeship to Tocasia". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia is revealed as the likely inventor of the Grapeshot Catapult creatures used by both brothers.
timeline.quote: invented by Urza's and Mishra's original master, Tocasia, and that both brothers used them

citation.text: Grapeshot Catapult (Fourth Edition, 1995), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Urza applies Tocasia's lessons on resource gathering.
timeline.quote: Urza always put Tocasia's lessons on resource-gathering to effective use.

citation.text: Urza's Tower (Chronicles, 1995), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Research suggests Tocasia invented the Grapeshot Catapult used by both brothers.
timeline.quote: Recent research suggests these creatures were invented by Urza's and Mishra's original master, Tocasia, and that both brothers used them.

citation.text: Grapeshot Catapult (Fifth Edition, 1997), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The brothers and Tocasia discover Koilos, the secret heart of Thran civilization.
timeline.quote: In AR 20 the brothers and Tocasia discover Koilos

citation.text: "The Brothers' War (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A drunken Mishra fights Urza with their powerstones, and the resulting explosion kills Tocasia.
timeline.quote: the area explodes, killing her

citation.text: "The Brothers' War (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia teaches two brothers a lesson on raw elemental magic.
timeline.quote: she began a lesson on raw elemental magic.

citation.text: Primal Plasma (Planar Chaos, 2007), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Mishra comes to despise Tocasia.
timeline.quote: Though he eventually came to despise Tocasia

citation.text: Mishra's Workshop (Masters Edition IV, 2011), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Tocasia cleared her table and began a lesson on raw elemental magic for two brothers.
timeline.quote: Tocasia brushed the gears and cogs from the table.

citation.text: Primal Plasma (Planechase 2012, 2012), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Tocasia taught two brothers a lesson on raw elemental magic.
timeline.quote: There, before two wide-eyed brothers, she began a lesson on raw elemental magic.

citation.text: Primal Plasma (Time Spiral Remastered, 2021), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Urza comes to understand Tocasia's lessons and makes perfection his goal.
timeline.quote: Perfection became his goal, and all other matters fell away in its pursuit.

citation.text: Urza's Workshop (The Brothers' War Commander, 2022), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Tocasia welcomes a young person, saying their father wanted her to look after them.
timeline.quote: "Your father was a dear friend to whom I owe much."

citation.text: Tocasia's Welcome (The Brothers' War, 2022), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Mishra flees after the explosion that kills Tocasia, never looking back.
timeline.quote: Mishra kept running and never once looked back.

citation.text: Overwhelming Remorse (The Brothers' War, 2022), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: The brothers' rivalry becomes all-out enmity and Tocasia pays the price.
timeline.quote: The brothers' rivalry escalated into all-out enmity, and Tocasia paid the price.

citation.text: Brotherhood's End (The Brothers' War, 2022), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Urza, Tocasia and Mishra find the caves and a large powerstone; they claim halves, accidentally open the portal, and flee su-chi attackers.
timeline.quote: However, they unwittingly opened the portal between Dominaria and Phyrexia and were attacked by su-chi

citation.text: "Koilos", section "Brothers’ War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Tocasia dies when hit by energy beams from the split stones.
timeline.quote: She dies when hit by energy beams from the stones.

citation.text: "Timeline", section "The Brothers' War (20 AR to 64 AR) [ 16 ] [ 50 ]". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The brothers and Tocasia discover Koilos, and the brothers split a powerstone, creating the Mightstone and Weakstone.
timeline.quote: The brothers split a Thran powerstone , accidentally creating the Mightstone and Weakstone .

citation.text: "Timeline/The Brothers' War", section "Prelude". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A conflict between the brothers kills Tocasia in an explosion; Mishra flees and is enslaved by Fallaji nomads while Urza apprentices to Rusko.
timeline.quote: A conflict between the brothers arises, with Tocasia accidentally caught in between and killed in an explosion.

citation.text: "Timeline/The Brothers' War", section "Prelude". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After 5,000 years Urza, Mishra and Tocasia rediscover the caves, and Urza renames them Koilos.
timeline.quote: They then received the new name " Koilos " from Urza.

citation.text: "Caves of the Damned", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Urza and Mishra rework salvaged Thran thopters, which serve as transport throughout the Brothers' War.
timeline.quote: Thopters were among the first devices worked upon by the brothers Urza and Mishra .

citation.text: "Thopter", section "Dominaria". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

relations.quote: Loran was the true heir to her legacy.

citation.text: Loran, Disciple of History (The Brothers' War, 2022), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.
